prompt:
Build a closed-loop ECMO-assisted cardiovascular circulation model using Simulink and Simscape physical networks. A pulsatile heart must drive systemic and pulmonary resistance, inertance, and compliance paths, while a venous blood path must pass through an actively commanded pump and oxygenator before returning to the arterial circulation. Read the scalar base-workspace variables target_map_initial_mmHg, target_map_final_mmHg, target_step_time_s, systemic_resistance_scale, heart_rate_bpm, and pump_speed_limit_rpm. Their nominal values are 115 mmHg, 120 mmHg, 2.5 s, 1.0, 75 beats/min, and 4500 rpm; their allowed ranges are 110-120 mmHg, 112-124 mmHg, 2.0-3.0 s, 0.75-1.30, 60-100 beats/min, and 3500-5000 rpm, respectively. Assume a clean MATLAB session in which only these declared public inputs are provided; every other parameter and initialization dependency must be self-contained in the saved model. Across the declared operating range, use physically measured aortic pressure as feedback to command the real ECMO pump so that beat-averaged aortic pressure follows the requested initial value and the requested step to the final value, while maintaining forward ECMO flow and physically consistent systemic and pulmonary circulation. Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries pressure_state with three channels ordered as aortic pressure, central venous pressure, and pulmonary arterial pressure in mmHg; flow_state with three channels ordered as ECMO flow, systemic arterial flow, and pulmonary arterial flow in cm^3/s, positive in their physical forward directions; and pump_command with the commanded pump speed in rpm. All pressure and flow channels must originate from the corresponding physical measurement locations, not from references or constructed answer waveforms. Work directly in cand_XMED02.slx and keep the latest usable state saved at that path throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XMED02.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
